research_rationale:
Executive Order 13876 of June 24, 2019 (84 FR 30573), Imposing Sanctions With Respect to Iran, has eleven sections. The held Federal Register text layer (jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_13876.txt, 84 FR 30573, PDF pages 1-4) carries the heading, the date June 24, 2019 and FR Doc. 2019-13793. The order takes additional steps with respect to the national emergency declared in Executive Order 12957. It blocks the property of the Supreme Leader and his Office and of persons determined under five criteria (section 1), authorizes correspondent-account sanctions on foreign financial institutions (section 2), prohibits donations (section 3) and lists conduct the prohibitions include (section 4), suspends entry of covered aliens (section 5), delegates implementation to the Treasury (section 6), prohibits evasion and conspiracy (section 7), defines terms (section 8), finds that no prior notice is needed (section 9), and has general provisions (section 10) and a statement that the measures respond to Iran's post-Algiers Accords actions (section 11). The dossier's 28 clauses cover these and are accepted. The order states no end date or condition. The emergency was continued each March through the notice of March 2, 2026, and Executive Order 14382 of 2026 builds on the same emergency without touching this order. A search of the held corpus for the number EO 13876 (20 files) finds the order, the continuation notices that list it, OFAC rules and notices, 31 CFR part 561 and 22 U.S.C. 8501 note; the only revoke-wording near the number is the notices' recital about Executive Orders 13716 and 13628, which concerns other orders (see the conflict resolution). The status on 2026-10-14 is operative for all 28 clauses. The held text is a machine-extracted text layer of the official PDF; page images were not inspected.
